extraction.name: CIFAR-10
extraction.description: The CIFAR-10 dataset contains 60,000 32x32 color images, each labeled as one of ten classes. It is divided into a training set of 50,000 images and a validation set of 10,000 images.
extraction.creator: Krizhevsky et al.
extraction.citeAs: Keller Jordan. 94% on CIFAR-10 in 3.29 Seconds on a Single GPU. arXiv:2404.00498v2 [cs.LG], 2024.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images are manipulated through horizontal flipping augmentation (both random and alternating variants), 2-pixel random translation with reflection padding, and for the 96% accuracy target, 12-pixel Cutout augmentation is applied. Test-time augmentation includes horizontal flipping and multiple crops (untranslated, translated up-and-to-the-left by one pixel, translated down-and-to-the-right by one pixel, and mirrored versions of all three).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For data augmentation we use random horizontal flipping alongside 2-pixel random translation. For translation we use reflection padding which we found to be better than zero-padding. We propose to modify standard random horizontal flipping augmentation as follows. For the first epoch, we randomly flip 50% of inputs as usual. Then on epochs {2,4,6,...}, we flip only those inputs which were not flipped in the first epoch, and on epochs {3,5,7,...}, we flip only those inputs which were flipped in the first epoch.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The training methods are specifically optimized for CIFAR-10 and may not generalize to other datasets without additional tuning. The paper notes that standard ImageNet trainings considered do not significantly benefit from horizontal flipping augmentation. The methods require specific hardware (NVIDIA A100 GPU) to achieve the reported training speeds. The 94% accuracy target represents human-level performance as reported by Karpathy (2011), but the methods' performance on distribution shifts or out-of-distribution data is not discussed.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation. The dataset is used for training neural networks to reach specific accuracy targets (94%, 95%, 96%) and evaluating model performance. It is divided into a training set of 50,000 images and a validation set of 10,000 images.
